subject.title: feat(exec): verified-human instruction provenance for sensitive targets

question: What verified-human provenance contract and sensitive-target enforcement surface should OpenClaw support for exec, gateway mutations, and outbound messages?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates a new security boundary plus config/API semantics; automation cannot safely choose the provenance definition, fallback behavior, plugin visibility, or compatibility posture.

options.title: Core Gateway Policy
options.body: Define core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit provenance propagation and deny-or-approval fallback for exec, gateway mutations, and high-risk outbound sends.

options.title: Plugin Facts First
options.body: First land additive hook/action/provenance facts so a trusted security plugin can implement the policy before core owns default enforcement.

options.title: Fold Into Taint Umbrella
options.body: Defer this specific request into the broader persistent-taint and content-derived execution design so maintainers choose one unified security model.

recommendation.title: Core Gateway Policy
recommendation.body: Define core-enforced sensitive-target policy with explicit provenance propagation and deny-or-approval fallback for exec, gateway mutations, and high-risk outbound sends.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is recent work on tool-veto security events and exec approval policy surfaces, where the policy contract would likely be reviewed.
